note.explanation: Living things are organized from small, simple parts to larger, more complex levels. Parts at each level work together, so higher levels can do things their separate parts cannot do alone.
examples: Muscle cells work together to form muscle tissue, which can contract and generate force.
Different tissues in the heart work together so the heart can pump blood.
note.simple: Small parts join together to make bigger parts. When the parts work together, the bigger structure can do more.
note.title: Levels of organization
steps: Organs work together in organ systems.
Organ systems together make an organism.
note.answer: The levels from simplest to most complex are atom, molecule, organelle, cell, tissue, organ, organ system, and organism.

A group of molecules working together
A group of organs working together
A living entity made of organ systems
rationales: Correct: a tissue is a group of similar cells working together to perform specific functions.
Incorrect: molecules combine in specific ways to make organelles, not tissues.
Incorrect: multiple organs working together make an organ system.

mcqs.stem: A structure made up of related tissues working together is a(n):
rationales: Incorrect: a cell is made when organelles assemble and interact.
Incorrect: a tissue is a group of similar cells.
Correct: related tissues working together make an organ.
Incorrect: multiple organs working together make an organ system.

mcqs.stem: Which sequence correctly shows the order from the smallest of these levels to the largest?
rationales: Correct: atoms form molecules, molecules form organelles, and organelles assemble in cells.
Incorrect: molecules are made of atoms, and organelles form before cells.
Incorrect: this sequence reverses the levels from cell down to atom.
Incorrect: molecules are made of atoms, and organelles are made from molecules.

mcqs.stem: Which pair consists of animal organs?
rationales: Incorrect: xylem and phloem are examples of plant vascular tissues.
Incorrect: mitochondria and ribosomes are organelles.
Correct: the heart and lungs are examples of animal organs.
Incorrect: root system and shoot system are plant organ systems.

mcqs.stem: Which plant tissue transports water and nutrients?
rationales: Incorrect: epidermal tissue protects the underlying parts of a plant.
Correct: vascular tissue, including xylem and phloem, transports water and nutrients.
Incorrect: muscle tissue enables movement in animals.
Incorrect: epithelial tissue covers body surfaces and lines cavities in animals.

options: Tissues can perform only the functions of their individual cells.
Interactions between parts can produce functions not possible in the individual parts.
Higher levels are always simpler than lower levels.
Organ systems work independently of organs.
mcqs.stem: What is meant by an emergent property?
rationales: Incorrect: the section explains that tissues can have properties not present in their individual cells.
Correct: interactions among components can create new functions at a higher level.
Incorrect: higher levels of organization are increasingly complex.
Incorrect: organ systems consist of organs that work together.

mcqs.stem: Which is an example of an animal organ system that breaks down food and absorbs nutrients?
rationales: Correct: the digestive system breaks down food and absorbs nutrients.
Incorrect: the circulatory system transports nutrients and oxygen through the body.
Incorrect: the root system anchors a plant and absorbs water and nutrients.
Incorrect: the shoot system supports the plant and conducts photosynthesis.

mcqs.stem: Which choice is the highest level of organization in this list?
rationales: Incorrect: mitochondria are organelles.
Incorrect: cardiac muscle is a tissue.
Incorrect: the heart is an organ.
Correct: an organ system is above the organ level.

written.text: Explain the levels of organization in multicellular organism. How does each level contribute to the overall functioning of an organism?
written.finalAnswer: Atoms form molecules; molecules form organelles; organelles work together in cells; similar cells form tissues; related tissues form organs; organs work together in organ systems; and organ systems together make an organism. Each level contributes by combining with other parts to perform increasingly complex functions.

modelAnswer: Atoms are the smallest unit of matter that maintain the property of an element.
Atoms combine to form molecules.
Molecules combine in specific ways to make organelles, each specialized for a particular function.
Organelles assemble and interact to make cells, the smallest units with characteristics of life.
Similar cells work together in tissues to perform specific functions.
Related tissues work together in organs to perform specific functions.
Multiple organs work together in organ systems to perform related functions.
Organ systems together make an organism.
Each higher level combines the activities of lower levels to perform increasingly complex functions.
Answer: Atom → molecule → organelle → cell → tissue → organ → organ system → organism.

written.text: What is a tissue level? Explain plant and animal tissues.
written.finalAnswer: A tissue is a group of similar cells that work together to perform one or more specific functions. In animals, epithelial tissue covers body surfaces and lines cavities, while muscle tissue enables movement. In plants, epidermal tissue protects underlying parts, while vascular tissue transports water and nutrients.

modelAnswer: A tissue is a group of similar cells that work together to perform one or more specific functions.
In animals, epithelial tissue covers body surfaces and lines cavities.

Answer: Animal tissues include epithelial and muscle tissue; plant tissues include epidermal and vascular tissue, each performing its specific function.

written.text: Evaluate the importance of organ systems working in harmony and predict the consequences of a failure in one system on the others.
written.finalAnswer: Organ systems work together to carry out vital functions and allow an organism to function. If one system fails, the coordinated work of other systems can be disrupted, so they may not perform their functions properly and the organism may be unable to function normally.

Answer: Organ systems must work in harmony; failure in one system can disrupt others and affect the whole organism.

examTips: A short question may ask you to list the levels of organization. Learn their correct order and do not skip cell or tissue.
For a definition question, use the textbook wording: a tissue is similar cells working together; an organ is related tissues working together; an organ system is multiple organs working together.
A longer question may ask you to explain how levels build on one another. Give the sequence and add what each level is made from or does.
For an emergent-properties question, explain that interactions between parts produce functions that individual parts cannot perform alone, and use a textbook example such as the heart pumping blood.

explain.title: The levels build on one another
explain.body: Organization starts with atoms and becomes more complex at each level: molecules, organelles, cells, tissues, organs, organ systems, and organisms.

explain.title: Cells and tissues
explain.body: A cell is the smallest unit with characteristics of life. A tissue is a group of similar cells that work together to perform one or more specific functions.

explain.title: Organs and organ systems
explain.body: An organ is made of related tissues working together. An organ system consists of multiple organs working together to perform related functions.

explain.title: Emergent properties
explain.body: When parts interact at a higher level, they can create functions that the separate parts cannot perform alone. For example, different heart tissues work together so the heart can pump blood.

explain.title: Examples in plants and animals
explain.body: In animals, the heart is an organ and the circulatory system is an organ system. In plants, a leaf is an organ, while the root system and shoot system are organ systems.

mistakes: Do not place tissue before cell: similar cells combine to form a tissue.
Do not define an organ as a group of similar cells; an organ consists of related tissues.
Do not confuse an organ system with an organ: an organ system contains multiple organs.
Do not leave out organelle when writing the complete sequence from atom to organism.
Do not describe emergent properties as functions of separate parts alone; they arise from the parts interacting.
